title: Laredo College Board Position 9 Heads to Dec. 12 Runoff as Vela, Lopez Advance
excerpt: Laredo College will hold a runoff election on Saturday, Dec. 12, to decide who fills Position 9 on its Board of Trustees, after no candidate won a majority on Nov. 3. Early voting runs Nov. 30 through Dec. 8.
content:
Laredo College will hold a runoff election on Saturday, Dec. 12, to decide who fills Position 9 on the Laredo College District Board of Trustees, after no candidate won a majority in the Nov. 3 general election, according to the college.

Early voting runs Monday, Nov. 30, through Tuesday, Dec. 8. More information is available on the college's elections website at go.laredo.edu/elections.

Under Texas Education Code Section 130.082(g) and Laredo College Board Policy BBBB, a candidate must receive a majority of the votes cast to win outright. When no one does, the two candidates with the most votes advance to a runoff.

Unofficial results from Nov. 3 put incumbent Ernestina "Tita" C. Vela first with 20,322 votes, or about 42 percent, followed by Eduardo Lopez with 16,217 votes, or about 34 percent. Priscilla Pantoja Johnson finished third with 11,816 votes, or about 24 percent.

Vela has served on the board for 12 years. Lopez is an educator with a doctorate in education and more than 24 years of experience who works for the Laredo Independent School District.

Laredo College President Dr. Minita Ramírez thanked voters for turning out "in historic numbers" and asked the community "to once again take part in this important process during the runoff election."

Board President Esteban Rangel also encouraged voters "to once again make their voices heard in the runoff election."

The runoff is expected to cost between $88,000 and $90,000, split between Laredo College and the City of Laredo, according to KGNS reporting.

Sources: Laredo College, "Runoff election set for Laredo College Board of Trustees Position 9," Nov. 9, 2026. laredo.edu; Local National, "Laredo mayor's race goes to runoff as Cuellar, Webb County Democrats win and Proposition 1 passes," Nov. 4, 2026. localnational.com; WiseVoter, "Laredo College Board Race Heads to Runoff," Nov. 5, 2026. wisevoter.com
